text: To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: These are the words of him who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks among the seven golden lampstands:
I know your works, your labor and your endurance. I know that you cannot tolerate wicked people, that you have tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and have found them false.

versions.text: I know your works, your labor and your endurance. I know that you cannot tolerate evil, that you have tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and have found them false.
versions.explanation: κακούς is a masculine plural adjective referring to evil persons, not abstract 'evil.' The context (testing false apostles) confirms that people are meant. Rendering it as 'evil' also weakens the link to the following clause.

text: You have endured; you have borne up for the sake of my name and have not grown weary.
But I have this against you: you have abandoned the love you had at first.
Remember, then, how far you have fallen. Repent, and do the works you did at first. If not, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
Yet this you have in your favor: you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give the right to eat from the tree of life, which stands in the paradise of God.
And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write: These are the words of the First and the Last, who was dead and came to life:
I know your affliction and your poverty—yet you are rich—and the slander of those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Look, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison to be tested, and you will suffer affliction for ten days. Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who conquers will never be harmed by the second death.
And to the angel of the church in Pergamum write: These are the words of him who has the sharp, double-edged sword:

I know where you live—where Satan's throne is. Yet you hold fast to my name, and you did not deny your faith in me even in the days of Antipas, my faithful witness, who was killed among you, where Satan lives.

But I have a few things against you: you have there some who hold to the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the people of Israel, so that they ate food sacrificed to idols and committed sexual immorality.
So you too have some among you who hold in the same way to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.

versions.text: In the same way, you also have some who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
versions.explanation: The verse contains both οὕτως and ὁμοίως, stressing that the Nicolaitan error matches Balaam's; the current rendering drops one of the two markers. Recasting keeps the emphatic comparison while remaining smooth for reading aloud.

text: So repent. If not, I will come to you soon and wage war against them with the sword of my mouth.

Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone with a new name written on it, known only to the one who receives it.
And to the angel of the church in Thyatira write: These are the words of the Son of God, whose eyes are like blazing fire and whose feet are like burnished bronze:
I know your works—your love and faith, your service and endurance—and that your latest works are greater than your first.
But I have this against you: you tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. She teaches and misleads my servants into sexual immorality and the eating of food sacrificed to idols.

versions.text: But I have this against you: you tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophet. By her teaching she leads my servants astray into sexual immorality and the eating of food sacrificed to idols.
versions.explanation: The Greek has two coordinated verbs, 'she teaches and leads astray,' rather than the instrumental 'by her teaching'; keeping both verbs preserves the force of the accusation and reads well aloud. Also προφῆτιν is feminine ('prophetess'), which matters here since the whole charge concerns this woman's self-designation.

text: I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to turn from her immorality.
Look, I am throwing her onto a bed of suffering, and those who commit adultery with her into terrible affliction, unless they repent of her works.

versions.text: Look, I am throwing her onto a bed of sickness, and those who commit adultery with her into terrible affliction, unless they repent of her works.
versions.explanation: The Greek says only 'I am throwing her onto a bed'; 'sickness' names a specific diagnosis that the text does not. 'Bed of suffering' keeps the implied judgment without adding a medical detail, and it parallels the 'affliction' of the next clause.

text: I will strike her children dead, and all the churches will know that I am the one who searches hearts and minds, and I will repay each of you according to your works.
But to the rest of you in Thyatira, who do not hold this teaching and have not learned what they call the deep things of Satan, I say: I lay on you no other burden.
Only hold fast to what you have until I come.
To the one who conquers and keeps my works to the end, I will give authority over the nations—
he will rule them with an iron rod and shatter them like clay pots—
just as I myself have received authority from my Father. And I will give him the morning star.
Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
